bg: Spain

Paul expresses his intention (Rom. 15:24, 28) to visit Spain. There is, however, no evidence that he ever carried it into effect, although some think that he probably did so between his first and second imprisonment.
Asia

Is used to denote Proconsular Asia, a Roman province which embraced the western parts of Asia Minor, and of which Ephesus was the capital, in Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10, 22; 20:4, 16, 18, etc., and probably Asia Minor in Acts 19:26, 27; 21:27; 24:18; 27:2. Proconsular Asia contained the seven churches of the Apocalypse (Rev. 1:11).

ch.s: Verses 1–10: “In the one hundred seventy-second year, King Demetrius gathered his forces together, and went into Media to get help, that he might fight against Tryphon.”; Verses 11–20: “He made peace in the land, and Israel rejoiced with great joy.”; Verses 21–30: “The ambassadors who were sent to our people reported to us about your glory and honor. We were glad for their coming”; Verses 31–40: “Their enemies planned to invade their country, that they might destroy their country utterly, and stretch out their hands against their sanctuary.”; Verses 41–49: “and that the Jews and the priests were well pleased that Simon should be their leader and high priest forever, until there should arise a faithful prophet”. People named: Simon, Demetrius, Jonathan, Rome, Tryphon, Judas. Places: Jerusalem, Media, Joppa, Persia, No.
q: Read verses 1–10. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 11–20, what do you learn about leadership and kingship?
Read verse 29 slowly. What does it say about God, about people, and about how to live?
What does Simon’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of family and generations in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 Maccabees?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Write down three things this chapter shows about God and thank Him for each.

bg: Dor
Dwelling, the Dora of the Romans, an ancient royal city of the Canaanites (Josh. 11:1, 2; 12:23). It was the most southern settlement of the Phoenicians on the coast of Syria.

bg: Azotus
The Grecized form (Acts 8:40, etc.) of Ashdod (q.v.).
ch.s: Verses 1–6: “John went up from Gazara and told Simon his father what Cendebaeus was doing.”; Verses 7–12: “He divided the people, and placed the cavalry in the midst of the infantry; but the enemies’ cavalry were exceedingly many.”; Verses 13–18: “His heart was lifted up, and he planned to make himself master of the country, and he made deceitful plans against Simon and his sons, to do away…”; Verses 19–24: “He sent others to Gazara to do away with John. To the captains of thousands, he sent letters to come to him, that he might give them silver…”. People named: John, Simon, Judas, Mattathias, Sebat. Places: Jericho, Kidron, Azotus, Jerusalem.
